# Results — Study 349 (Regime-Dependence) on real canonical strategies

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The regime-dependence lens
applied to two canonical strategies on a real US tape: a **12-month time-series-momentum
(trend) overlay** on the equity index, and a **static 60/40 stock/bond mix**. Each is
split by decade; we report the decade-conditional Sharpe, the stability score, and the
**danger number** — the Sharpe and HAC t with the single best decade removed. Monthly
total-return data. As-of **2026-05-31** (the last full month — the in-progress June bar is
dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Equity leg | `^SP500TR` (S&P 500 total return) |
| Bond leg | `IEF` (7–10y US Treasuries ETF, total return) |
| Window | 2002-08-31 → 2026-05-31 (286 months) |
| Fingerprint | `1573a701e3bd` |
| Source | Yahoo! Finance, total-return monthly |

> **The bond leg caps the history.** `IEF` only lists from 2002, so the real tape spans
> *three* decades (2000s, 2010s, 2020s), not the five-plus the synthetic control uses. With
> only three regimes the cross-regime difference test is low-powered — a documented
> limitation, not a hidden one. The trend overlay (equity-only) could run longer; we hold
> both to the same window so the two strategies are comparable.

## The headline — decade-by-decade Sharpe (gross, total return)

| Strategy | full-sample Sharpe | HAC *t* | 2000s | 2010s | 2020s | stability CV | drop-best-decade Sharpe → | HAC *t* → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Trend (12m TSMOM)** | +0.90 | +4.54 | +0.97 | +0.89 | +0.94 | **0.04** | +0.91 | **+3.84** |
| **Static 60/40** | +0.97 | +5.09 | +0.66 | **+1.46** | +0.86 | **0.34** | +0.76 | **+2.92** |

- **The trend overlay is genuinely regime-robust.** Its Sharpe is ~0.9 in *every* decade
  (CV 0.04), and removing its best decade barely moves it (0.90 → 0.91, HAC *t* still
  +3.84). This is what a durable edge looks like under the lens.
- **The 60/40 "ruled the 2010s."** Its 2010s Sharpe (+1.46) towers over the 2000s (+0.66)
  and 2020s (+0.86) — CV 0.34, eight times the trend's. Removing the 2010s drops the
  Sharpe 0.97 → 0.76 and the HAC *t* 5.09 → 2.92. The edge **survives** the loss of its
  best decade (still *t* > 2), but it leaned heavily on one era.
- **Neither real strategy is a regime-fitted mirage** — both clear *t* ≥ 2 with their best
  decade removed. The best-decade-minus-rest gap CIs straddle zero on this short tape
  (trend [−16.2, +5.9]%/yr, 60/40 [−5.4, +10.3]%/yr), so with only three regimes the
  apparent decade-to-decade variation is **not statistically resolvable** — a power
  limitation, named.

## The synthetic control — the lens catches a regime-fitted strategy

The danger the lens is built to catch does not show up cleanly in these two well-worn real
strategies, so we prove the machinery on a deterministic tape where the ground truth is
*planted*. Two strategies on the same six-regime market: a **durable** edge present in
every regime, and a **regime-fitted** edge present in only one. Crucially, the
regime-fitted strategy's **full-sample Sharpe (0.41) is as good as or better than** the
durable one's (0.34) — a single number cannot tell them apart.

| Strategy (synthetic) | full-sample Sharpe | stability CV | share in best regime | drop-best-regime Sharpe → | HAC *t* → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Durable (edge every regime) | 0.34 | 0.42 | 26% | 0.30 | **+2.14** (survives) |
| Regime-fitted (edge one regime) | **0.41** | **1.02** | **55%** | 0.22 | **+1.56** (collapses) |

- The regime-fitted strategy **looks better** on the headline Sharpe, yet earns **55%** of
  its edge in a single regime; remove that regime and its HAC *t* falls from significant to
  **1.56** — below the bar. The durable strategy, with the *lower* headline Sharpe, **keeps**
  its *t* > 2 with its best regime removed.
- The cross-regime gap CI for the regime-fitted strategy is **[+4.5, +33.8]%/yr — entirely
  above zero**, correctly flagging the concentration; the durable strategy's gap straddles
  zero ([−14.7, +20.2]). The lens reverses the headline ranking and is a faithful detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** A methodology demo certifies no tradable effect, and on the real tape
  the apparent decade-to-decade Sharpe differences are *not* resolvable from noise with only
  three regimes (gap CIs straddle zero). There is no real-tape regime pathology to stamp
  `REAL`; the synthetic control is a machinery proof, never market evidence.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The product is a *measuring instrument*, not a strategy — there
  is nothing here to buy. (And the lesson it teaches kills strategies; it does not mint
  alpha.)
- **Did ruling one decade prove skill? — IT DEPENDS, and the lens tells you which.**
  *Confirmed on synthetic ground truth:* a strategy can post a top-tier full-sample Sharpe
  while owing more than half its edge to one regime, and a single Sharpe will never reveal
  it. The fix — decade-conditional Sharpe, the drop-best-decade re-estimate, and a
  cross-regime gap CI — correctly separates a durable edge from a one-era bet. On the real
  canonical strategies, the trend overlay passes cleanly (CV 0.04); the 60/40 leaned on the
  2010s but still survived its removal (*t* = 2.92). Fit to one era, and a backtest will lie
  to you — *unless* you split by regime first.
